counterevidence: One router's list prices, prompt tokens only; METR's horizon is software tasks under its suite, not general capability; the cheapest model per horizon-hour is a moving target as models are added.
definition: For each price date, the lowest OpenRouter prompt price (USD per million tokens) divided by the model's latest METR 50% time horizon in hours, across models present in both datasets. Derived metric frontier_price_per_horizon_hour.

direction_rule.rationale: Four price change-points; a move under two cents per million tokens per horizon-hour is noise. Rising = labs keeping the surplus from capability gains.

name: Price per unit of capability (cheapest METR-hour on OpenRouter)
stale_reason: Change-point series: a quiet month means prices held; fetch freshness is on /sources.

status_events.author: evaluate
status_events.reason: First price snapshot, 10 Sep 2026: the cheapest METR-measured capability on OpenRouter costs about $0.30 per million prompt tokens per hour of 50% time horizon (16 models present in both datasets). The series records price change-points, so a direction needs four more of them; not yet measurable until then. Initial seed.

timing_rationale: Coincident: list prices change the day a lab reprices or releases, the moment capability becomes purchasable.
tracker_interpretation: The series records price change-points from 10 September 2026; a direction needs several months of them.
why_it_matters: Price per unit of capability is the lab layer's capture proxy. Falling means the surplus from better models is passed to applications and users; flat or rising means labs keep it.
